1. Executive Summary & Problem Statement

In public procurement and infrastructure tenders across India, technical specifications must strictly adhere to Indian Standards (IS codes) formulated by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). Procurement officers frequently deal with complex requirement specifications (e.g., street lighting, TMT reinforced bars, electrical safety helmets). Manually searching standard catalogs is labor-intensive, error-prone, and causes compliance disputes.

This project implements an end-to-end cloud solution on Amazon Web Services (AWS) that allows users to submit natural-language requirements and instantly receive ranked, verified Indian Standards with real-time audit logging.

2. AWS Cloud Architecture & Technical Justification

AWS Service Role in Project Architectural Justification (AWS Well-Architected Framework)
AWS IAM Instance Profile Role (EC2-ProcurementApp-Role) Security Pillar: Enforces the Principle of Least Privilege. Temporary credentials are automatically assigned via IMDSv2 without storing secret keys in source code.
Amazon EC2 Compute Tier (Ubuntu 24.04, t3.micro) Performance & Reliability: Hosts Nginx reverse proxy, Gunicorn WSGI server, Django REST API, and Sentence Transformer vector inference with 2GB swap space.
Amazon S3 Dataset Storage (procurement-standards-bucket) Durability & Decoupling: Stores bis_data.json with 99.999999999% durability. Decouples dataset updates from server redeployments.
Amazon DynamoDB Audit Database (bis_search_logs) Operational Excellence: Low-latency NoSQL table recording real-time search queries, latency metrics, and retrieved standards with zero database management.

5. Viva Voce Defense Guide (Faculty Questions & Answers)

Q1: What are the 4 mandatory AWS services used in your project?

A: 1. AWS IAM (Role EC2-ProcurementApp-Role providing least-privilege access). 2. Amazon EC2 (Hosts Ubuntu, Nginx, Gunicorn, and AI inference). 3. Amazon S3 (Houses the bis_data.json standards dataset). 4. Amazon DynamoDB (Table bis_search_logs recording query audit logs).

Q2: Why did you choose Amazon DynamoDB over Amazon RDS?

A: Search audit logging is event-driven and write-intensive with semi-structured JSON payloads. DynamoDB provides single-digit millisecond latency, zero connection pool bottlenecks, seamless on-demand scaling, and 25 GB free tier storage without database management overhead.

Q3: How do you authenticate with AWS services securely?

A: Following the AWS Security Pillar, we use an IAM Instance Profile attached directly to EC2. The Boto3 SDK retrieves temporary rotating credentials from the Instance Metadata Service (IMDSv2). No AWS access keys or secret keys are stored in code or environment files.

Q4: How does your deployment handle Free Tier memory limits?

A: We provisioned a 2GB Linux swap file on the 20 GiB EBS disk, preventing Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors during Sentence Transformer model inference on t3.micro (1 GB RAM). Gunicorn is tuned to 1 worker with a 120-second timeout.
